“The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a king who made a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his slaves to call those invited to the wedding feast, but they were unwilling to come.
Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my meal. My bulls and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.’
But they disregarded it and went away, one to his own field, another to his business.
The rest seized his slaves, mistreated them, and killed them.
The king became angry. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Then he said to his slaves, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
So go to the outlets of the roads and invite to the wedding feast as many as you find.’
Those slaves went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, both evil and good, and the wedding feast was filled with people reclining.
The king entered to see those reclining and saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment.
He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you enter here without a wedding garment?’ He was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind his feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’
For many are called, but few chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how to trap Him in a statement.

They sent Him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that Thou art truthful and dost teach God’s way in truth. Thou art not swayed by anyone, for Thou dost not look at people’s outward status.
Tell us, then, what Thou thinkest: is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?”
Knowing their evil intent, Jesus said, “Why do you test Me, hypocrites?
Show Me the coin of the tribute.” And they brought Him a denarius.
And He says to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?”
They say to Him, “Caesar’s.” Then He says to them, “Render therefore to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God.”
When they heard, they marveled, left Him, and went away.
On that day Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and questioned Him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If someone dies without children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother.
Likewise the second and the third, up to the seventh.
Last of all, the woman died.
In the resurrection, then, whose wife of the seven will she be? For all had her.”
Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God:
‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not God of the dead, but of the living.”
When the crowds heard, they were astonished at His teaching.
Hearing that He had silenced the Sadducees, the Pharisees gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the Law, questioned Him to test Him:
“Teacher, which commandment is great in the Law?”
He said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
This is the great and first commandment.
A second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets.”
While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them,
saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” They said to Him, “David’s.”
He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord, saying,
‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I put Thy enemies beneath Thy feet’?
If David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?”
No one could answer Him a word, nor from that day did anyone dare question Him any longer.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and His disciples,
saying, “The scribes and Pharisees have seated themselves in Moses’ chair.
Therefore do and observe everything they tell you, but do not act according to their works, for they say and do not do.
They bind heavy burdens, hard to carry, and lay them upon people’s shoulders, but they themselves are unwilling to move them with their finger.
They do all their works to be seen by people. They broaden their phylacteries and enlarge their fringes.
They love the foremost place at dinners and the foremost seats in the synagogues,
greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
But you shall not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher, and you are all brothers.
And call no one upon earth your father, for One is your Father, the heavenly One.
Nor shall you be called guides, because One is your Guide, the Christ.
But the greatest among you will be your servant.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of the heavens before people! For you do not enter, nor do you permit those entering to enter.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves!
Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is bound.’
Fools and blind men! For which is greater, the gold or the sanctuary that sanctified the gold?
And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift upon it is bound.’
Blind men! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
Therefore the one swearing by the altar swears by it and by everything upon it.
The one swearing by the sanctuary swears by it and by the One dwelling in it.
The one swearing by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One seated upon it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have left aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have done without leaving those aside.
Blind guides, straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of plunder and self-indulgence!
Blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of the cup, so that its outside may also become clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you resemble whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead people’s bones and all uncleanness!
So you too outwardly appear righteous to people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the prophets’ tombs and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
and say, ‘If we had lived in our fathers’ days, we would not have shared with them in the blood of the prophets.’
So you testify concerning yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
You, then, fill up the measure of your fathers!
Snakes, brood of vipers! How will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?
Therefore behold, I send you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,

so that upon you may come all righteous blood poured out upon earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wished to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling!
Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
For I tell you, you will certainly not see Me from now until you say, ‘Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord.’”
Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, when His disciples came to show Him the temple buildings.
He answered them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down.”
As He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what is the sign of Thy coming and the consummation of the age?”
Jesus answered them, “See that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
You will hear wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
All these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.
Then many will stumble, hand one another over, and hate one another.
Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in a holy place—let the reader understand—
then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the housetop not go down to take things from his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
Woe to those with child and those nursing infants in those days!
Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath.
For then there will be great affliction such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and certainly will never happen again.
If those days had not been shortened, no flesh would have been saved; but because of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Behold, I have told you beforehand.
So if they tell you, ‘Behold, He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Behold, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
For just as lightning comes from the east and shines to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.
Concerning that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
For just as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
They did not know until the flood came and took them all away. So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.
Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.
So keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord comes.
But know this: if the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man comes at an hour you do not expect.
Who, then, is the faithful and prudent slave whom the master appointed over his household to give them food at the proper time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
Truly I tell you that he will appoint him over all his belongings.
But if that evil slave says in his heart, ‘My master delays,’
and begins to beat his fellow slaves and eats and drinks with drunkards,
the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.
He will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish and five prudent.
For the foolish took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
The prudent took oil in containers along with their lamps.
As the bridegroom delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.
At midnight a cry arose: ‘Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’
Then all those virgins arose and put their lamps in order.
The foolish said to the prudent, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’
The prudent answered, ‘There may not be enough for us and you. Go instead to those selling and buy for yourselves.’
While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’
He answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
For it is like a man traveling abroad, who called his own slaves and handed over his belongings to them.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, each according to his own ability, and traveled abroad. Immediately
the one who received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.
Likewise the one with two gained another two.
But the one who received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master’s silver.
After a long time, the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.
The one who received five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over five talents to me. Look, I gained another five talents.’
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’
The one with two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you handed over two talents to me. Look, I gained another two talents.’
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’
The one who received one talent also came and said, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter.
I was afraid, so I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.’
His master answered him, ‘Evil and idle slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?
Then you ought to have deposited my silver with the bankers, and when I came I would have recovered what is mine with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken.
Cast the useless slave into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’
When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.
All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.
Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,
naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’
Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?
When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?
When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,
I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’
Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’
And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
When Jesus finished all these words, He said to His disciples,
“You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest called Caiaphas.
They took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill Him.
But they said, “Not during the feast, lest an uproar occur among the people.”
While Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to Him with an alabaster flask of very costly perfume and poured it upon His head as He reclined at table.
Seeing it, the disciples became indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
Knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work toward Me.
For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.
By pouring this perfume upon My body, she did it to prepare Me for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be told in remembrance of her.”
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?” They weighed out for him thirty silver coins.
From then on he sought a suitable opportunity to hand Him over.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Where dost Thou wish us to prepare for Thee to eat the Passover?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I keep the Passover at your house with My disciples.’”
The disciples did as Jesus directed them, and prepared the Passover.
When evening came, He reclined at table with the twelve.
As they ate, He said, “Truly I tell you that one of you will hand Me over.”
Exceedingly grieved, each began saying to Him, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand with Me in the dish will hand Me over.
The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written concerning Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born.”
Judas, who was handing Him over, answered, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”
And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed, He broke it; and giving it to the disciples, He said, “Take, eat; this is My body.”
And He took a cup, and having given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you;
for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins.
And I tell you: from this time I shall by no means drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father.”
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered Him, “Even if everyone stumbles because of Thee, I will never stumble.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you that this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
Peter said to Him, “Even if I must die with Thee, I will certainly not deny Thee.” All the disciples said likewise.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to be grieved and distressed.
Then He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Remain here and keep watch with Me.”
Going forward a little, He fell upon His face and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Nevertheless, not as I wish, but as Thou wishest.”
He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “So, could you not keep watch with Me for one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again He went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let Thy will be done.”
He came and again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
He left them and went away again, praying a third time and saying the same words again.
Then He came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is handed over into sinners’ hands.
Rise, let us go. Behold, the one handing Me over has drawn near.”
While He was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
The one handing Him over had given them a sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He; seize Him.”
Immediately he came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed Him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid their hands upon Jesus, and seized Him.
And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Return your sword to its place, for all who take a sword will perish by a sword.
Or do you think I cannot plead with My Father, and He will provide Me at once more than twelve legions of angels?
How, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?”
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to arrest Me? Daily I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize Me.
But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left Him and fled.
Those who seized Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Peter followed Him at a distance as far as the high priest’s courtyard. Going inside, he sat with the officers to see the outcome.
The chief priests and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus to put Him to death,
but found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
and said, “This Man said, ‘I can destroy God’s sanctuary and build it in three days.’”
The high priest rose and said to Him, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is this that they testify against Thee?”
But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to Him, “I adjure Thee by the living God to tell us whether Thou art the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Nevertheless I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right of the Power and coming upon the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you heard the blasphemy.
What do you think?” They answered, “He is liable to death.”
Then they spat into His face and struck Him with their fists; others slapped Him,
saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who struck Thee?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. One servant girl approached him, saying, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”
But he denied it before everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.”
When he went out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the Man.”
After a little while, those standing there came and said to Peter, “Truly you too are one of them, for even your speech makes you recognizable.”
Then he began to invoke curses and swear, “I do not know the Man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered Jesus’ word: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put Him to death.
They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, who had handed Him over, saw that He had been condemned. Filled with regret, he returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I sinned by handing over innocent blood.” They said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
He threw the silver coins into the sanctuary and withdrew; then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because they are the price of blood.”
After taking counsel, they bought the potter’s field with them as a burial place for strangers.
Therefore that field has been called Field of Blood until today.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price of the One priced, whom some of the sons of Israel priced,
and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” Jesus said, “You say it.”
While He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to Him, “Dost Thou not hear how many things they testify against Thee?”
He did not answer him even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
At the feast the governor customarily released to the crowd one prisoner whom they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
So when they gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus called Christ?”
For he knew that they had handed Him over because of envy.
While he sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous Man, for I suffered many things today in a dream because of Him.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
The governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus called Christ?” They all said, “Let Him be crucified!”
He said, “Why, what evil did He do?” But they cried out all the more, “Let Him be crucified!”
When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather an uproar was arising, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this blood. See to it yourselves.”
All the people answered, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”
Then he released Barabbas to them; after flogging Jesus, he handed Him over to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.
They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.
After mocking Him, they stripped off the cloak, dressed Him in His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.
As they went out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon. They compelled him to carry His cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,
and gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink. After tasting it, He was unwilling to drink.
After crucifying Him, they divided His garments by casting a lot,
and sat there keeping watch over Him.
Above His head they placed the written charge against Him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Then two robbers were crucified with Him, one at His right and one at His left.
Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads
and saying, “Thou who destroyest the sanctuary and buildest it in three days, save Thyself! If Thou art God’s Son, come down from the cross.”
Likewise the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,
“He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.
He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
The robbers crucified with Him also reproached Him in the same way.
From the sixth hour darkness came upon all the land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That is, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”
Some standing there heard and said, “This Man is calling Elijah.”
Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.
But the rest said, “Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save Him.”
Jesus again cried out with a loud voice and released His spirit.
And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised.
Coming out of the tombs after His rising, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
The centurion and those with him guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, and were exceedingly afraid, saying, “Truly this was God’s Son.”
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving Him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph came, who himself had also become Jesus’ disciple.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. Rolling a great stone to the tomb’s entrance, he went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
saying, “Sir, we remembered that while He was still alive, that deceiver said, ‘After three days I am raised.’

So command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest His disciples come, steal Him, and tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go and make it secure as you know how.”
They went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone, with the guard.
After the Sabbath, as it dawned toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to view the tomb.
And behold, a great earthquake occurred, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came, rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
From fear of him the guards shook and became like dead men.
The angel answered the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified.
He is not here, for He was raised, as He said. Come, see the place where He lay.
Go quickly and tell His disciples that He was raised from the dead; and behold, He goes ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see Him. Behold, I have told you.”
They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy and ran to report to His disciples.
And behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” They came, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him.
Then Jesus said to them, “Do not fear. Go and report to My brothers that they should go to Galilee, and there they will see Me.”
As they went, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
They gathered with the elders and took counsel, then gave a considerable amount of silver to the soldiers,
saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole Him while we slept.’
If this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him and make you free from worry.”
They took the silver and did as they were instructed. This account was spread among Jews until this very day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
When they saw Him, they worshiped, but some doubted.
And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and upon earth has been given to Me.
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep all that I commanded you; and behold, I am with you all the days, until the consummation of the age.”
The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way;
a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him. They were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and ate locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, saying, “The One stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals.
I baptized you with water, but He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
Immediately as He came up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending like a dove into Him.
A voice came from the heavens: “Thou art My beloved Son; in Thee I am well pleased.”
Immediately the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.
He was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God,
and saying, “The appointed time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent, and believe in the gospel.”
And passing beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.
And He said to them, “Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
Going a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in the boat, putting the nets in order.
Immediately He called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after Him.
They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath He went into the synagogue and taught.
They were astonished at His teaching, for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
“What have we to do with Thee, Jesus of Nazareth? Hast Thou come to destroy us? I know who Thou art—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be muzzled, and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit convulsed him, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
They were all amazed, so that they discussed among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching! With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him.”
Immediately the report about Him went out everywhere through the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
Immediately after leaving the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they told Him about her.
He came to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
When evening came, after the sun had set, they brought to Him all who were ill and those possessed by demons.
The whole city had gathered at the door.
He healed many who were ill with various diseases and cast out many demons. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
Very early, while it was still dark, He arose, went out, and departed to a deserted place, and there He prayed.
Simon and those with him searched for Him
and found Him. They said to Him, “Everyone is looking for Thee.”
He said to them, “Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for that is why I came out.”
He went throughout all Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out the demons.
A leper came to Him, pleading with Him, kneeling, and saying, “If Thou art willing, Thou canst cleanse me.”
And moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and says to him, “I will; be cleansed.”
Immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
Sternly warning him, He immediately drove him away
and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

But he went out and began proclaiming it widely and spreading the report, so that Jesus could no longer enter a city openly. He remained outside in deserted places, and they came to Him from every direction.
When He entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that He was at home.
Many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even near the door, and He was speaking the word to them.
They came, bringing to Him a paralyzed man carried by four men.
Since they could not bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they removed the roof above the place where He was. After digging through it, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man lay.
Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak this way? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except the one God?”
Immediately Jesus knew in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves. He said to them, “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Arise, take your mat, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—He said to the paralyzed man—
“I say to you, arise, take your mat, and go to your house.”
He arose, immediately took up the mat, and went out before everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
He went out again beside the sea. The whole crowd came to Him, and He taught them.
As He passed by, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax station. He said to him, “Follow Me.” He arose and followed Him.
As He reclined at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners reclined with Jesus and His disciples, for there were many who followed Him.
The scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with sinners and tax collectors and said to His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard and said to them, “The strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to Him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Thy disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the bridegroom’s companions fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old, and a worse tear results.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost along with the skins. New wine belongs in fresh wineskins.”
He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to make their way, plucking the heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to Him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him:
how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?”
And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
He entered a synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They watched Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, “Arise and come into the midst.”
He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill?” But they remained silent.
He looked around at them with anger, grieving at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea,
Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and the region of Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude heard all He was doing and came to Him.
He told His disciples to have a small boat ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him.
For He healed many, so that all who had afflictions pressed upon Him to touch Him.
Whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell before Him and cried, “Thou art the Son of God!”
He sternly warned them not to make Him known.
He went up the mountain and called to Himself those He wanted, and they came to Him.
He appointed twelve, whom He also named apostles, to be with Him and to be sent out by Him to proclaim
and to have authority to cast out the demons.
He appointed the Twelve: Simon, to whom He gave the name Peter;
James son of Zebedee and John, James’s brother, to whom He gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.
He came into a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
When His own people heard, they went out to take hold of Him, for they were saying, “He is out of His mind.”
The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons.”
He called them to Himself and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
If Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
No one can enter the strong man’s house and plunder his belongings unless he first binds the strong man. Then he will plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven everything—their sins and whatever blasphemies they may utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness for ever, but is liable for an eternal sin.”
For they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
His mother and His brothers came. Standing outside, they sent to Him and called Him.
A crowd was sitting around Him. They said to Him, “Look! Thy mother and Thy brothers and Thy sisters are outside looking for Thee.”
He answered them, “Who is My mother, or who are My brothers?”
He looked around at those sitting in a circle about Him and said, “Look—My mother and My brothers!
For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”
Again He began teaching beside the sea. A very great crowd gathered around Him, so that He got into a boat on the sea and sat down, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.
He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said to them:
“Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate it up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately sprang up because the soil had no depth.
When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Other seed fell among the thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
Other seeds fell into the good soil and gave fruit, growing up and increasing; they yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”
He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
When He was alone, those around Him, together with the Twelve, asked Him about the parables.
He said to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given. But for those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that, looking, they may look and not see, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest they turn back and be forgiven.”
He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones beside the road where the word is sown: whenever they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown into them.
Likewise, these are the ones sown on the rocky places: whenever they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
but they have no root in themselves and last only for a time. Then, when distress or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately stumble.
Others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who have heard the word,
but the cares of the age, the deceitfulness of riches, and desires for other things enter and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Those sown on the good soil are the ones who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”
He said to them, “Does the lamp come to be put under the modius basket, or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?
For nothing is hidden except to be revealed, nor has anything become secret except to come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
He said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
For whoever has will be given more; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.”
He said, “The kingdom of God is like this: a man casts seed on the ground,
and sleeps and rises, night and day, while the seed sprouts and grows—he himself does not know how.
The earth bears fruit of itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
When the crop is ready, he immediately sends in the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.”
He said, “How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we set it out?
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.
Yet when sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and makes great branches, so that the birds of the sky can shelter under its shade.”
With many such parables He spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear.
He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
On that day, when evening came, He said to them, “Let us cross to the other side.”
Leaving the crowd, they took Him with them, just as He was, in the boat. Other boats were with Him.
A great windstorm arose, and the waves broke into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.
He was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke Him and said to Him, “Teacher, dost Thou not care that we are perishing?”
And He awoke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be silent; be still.” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, “Why are you cowardly? Do you still have no faith?”
They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
They came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gerasenes.
As He stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit immediately met Him from the tombs.
He made his dwelling among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, even with a chain.
He had often been bound with fetters and chains, but he had torn the chains apart and shattered the fetters. No one had the strength to subdue him.
Continually, night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains, he cried out and cut himself with stones.
Seeing Jesus from far away, he ran and bowed before Him.
He cried out with a loud voice and said, “What hast Thou to do with me, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure Thee by God: do not torment me!”
For He had been saying to him, “Come out of the man, unclean spirit!”
He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to Him, “Legion is my name, because we are many.”
He begged Him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.
They begged Him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
He allowed them. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea—about two thousand—and they drowned in the sea.
Those tending them fled and reported it in the city and in the fields. People came to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and about the pigs.
They began begging Him to leave their territory.
As He was boarding the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged Him to let him be with Him.
He did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your own people and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how He has had mercy on you.”
He went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.
When Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him, and He was beside the sea.
One of the synagogue rulers came, named Jairus. Seeing Him, he fell at His feet
and begged Him earnestly, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay Thy hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”
He went with him. A large crowd followed Him and pressed against Him.
A woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered much under many physicians and spent everything she had, without any benefit but instead growing worse,
heard about Jesus. She came behind Him in the crowd and touched His garment.
For she was saying, “If I touch even His clothes, I will be saved.”
Immediately the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of the affliction.
Immediately Jesus, recognizing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched My clothes?”
His disciples said to Him, “Thou seest the crowd pressing against Thee, and Thou sayest, ‘Who touched Me?’”
He kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.
The woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell before Him and told Him the whole truth.
And He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be well, free from your affliction.”
While He was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further?”
Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, “Do not fear; only believe.”
He allowed no one to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
They came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and He saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went in and said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
They laughed at Him. But He put them all outside, took the child’s father and mother and those with Him, and went in where the child was.
Taking the child’s hand, He said to her, “Talitha koum,” which translated means, “Little girl, I say to you, arise!”
Immediately the little girl rose and walked around, for she was twelve years old. Immediately they were overcome with great amazement.
He gave them strict orders that no one should know this, and said that she should be given something to eat.
He left there and came to His hometown, and His disciples followed Him.

When the Sabbath came, He began teaching in the synagogue. The many who heard Him were astonished, saying, “Where did this Man get these things? What is this wisdom given to Him? And such mighty works taking place through His hands!
Is this not the carpenter, the Son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Are not His sisters here with us?” They took offense at Him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He could do no mighty work there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He marveled at their unbelief. Then He went around the surrounding villages, teaching.
He called the Twelve to Him and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bread, no bag, no copper money in their belt,
but to wear sandals, and, “Do not put on two tunics.”
He said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you leave that place.
Whatever place does not receive you, and whose people do not listen to you, shake off the dust beneath your feet as you leave there, as a testimony to them.”
They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
They cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
King Herod heard of it, for His name had become known. People were saying, “John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why mighty powers are at work in Him.”
Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard, he said, “John, whom I beheaded—he has been raised!”
For Herod himself had sent men to seize John and bind him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he listened to him gladly.
An opportune day came when Herod gave a dinner on his birthday for his dignitaries, commanders of thousands, and the leading men of Galilee.
His daughter Herodias came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those reclining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
He swore to her repeatedly, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She said, “The head of John the baptizer.”
Immediately she hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me at once, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.”
The king became deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table, he did not want to refuse her.
Immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John’s head. He went and beheaded him in prison,
brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl; the girl gave it to her mother.
When his disciples heard, they came and took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to Him everything they had done and taught.
He said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many were coming and going, and they did not even have an opportunity to eat.
They went away privately in the boat to a deserted place.
People saw them leaving, and many recognized them. They ran there together on foot from all the cities and arrived ahead of them.
As He stepped out, He saw a large crowd and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began teaching them many things.
When the hour was already late, His disciples came to Him and said, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late.
Dismiss them, so that they can go into the surrounding fields and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
He answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to Him, “Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
He ordered them to have everyone recline in dining groups on the green grass.
They reclined in rows, by hundreds and by fifties.

He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, pronounced a blessing, and broke the loaves. He kept giving them to His disciples to set before the people, and He divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
They took up broken pieces, twelve baskets full, and some of the fish.
Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.
Immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.
After saying farewell to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.
Seeing them straining at the rowing, for the wind was against them, He came toward them about the fourth watch of the night, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them.
When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out,
for they all saw Him and were troubled. Immediately He spoke with them and said to them, “Take courage! It is I; do not fear.”
He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. They were utterly astounded within themselves,
for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
When they crossed over to land, they came to Gennesaret and moored there.
As they stepped out of the boat, people immediately recognized Him
and ran through that whole country. They began carrying the sick around on their mats to wherever they heard He was.
Wherever He entered villages, cities, or fields, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him to let them touch even the fringe of His garment. As many as touched Him were saved.
The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Him.
They saw that some of His disciples were eating their bread with common hands—that is, unwashed.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders.
On returning from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves. There are many other things they received to observe: washings of cups, jugs, copper vessels, and couches.
The Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, “Why do Thy disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common hands?”
He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
In vain do they worship Me, teaching human commands for doctrine.’
You abandon God’s commandment and hold to human tradition.”
He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’
But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’
you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,
making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”
Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”
When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
He rose from there and went away into the territory of Tyre. He entered a house and wanted no one to know, but He could not remain hidden.
Immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, came, and fell at His feet.
The woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by birth. She asked Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
He said to her, “Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
She answered and said to Him, “Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat some of the children’s crumbs.”
He said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone out of your daughter.”
She went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
Leaving the territory of Tyre again, He came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the territory of the Decapolis.
They brought Him a man who was deaf and had difficulty speaking, and begged Him to lay His hand on him.
Taking him aside privately, away from the crowd, He put His fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.
Looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”
Immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke correctly.
He ordered them to tell no one. But the more He ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well! He even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.”
In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, He called the disciples to Him and said to them,
“I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with Me for three days and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home fasting, they will collapse on the way; and some of them have come from far away.”
His disciples answered Him, “Where can anyone get enough bread to satisfy these people here in a wilderness?”
He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, He gave thanks, broke them, and kept giving them to His disciples to set before the people; they set them before the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. He blessed them and said to set these before them as well.
They ate and were satisfied. They took up seven hampers of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand people. He dismissed them.
Immediately He boarded the boat with His disciples and came to the district of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out and began disputing with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, to test Him.
He sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
Leaving them, He boarded again and went away to the other side.
They had forgotten to take bread, and had only one loaf with them in the boat.
He warned them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”
They reasoned with one another that they had no bread.
Aware of this, He said to them, “Why are you reasoning that you have no bread? Do you not yet grasp or understand? Is your heart hardened?
Having eyes, do you not see? Having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces you took up?” They said to Him, “Twelve.”
“And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many hampers full of pieces did you take up?” They said to Him, “Seven.”
He said to them, “Do you not yet understand?”
They came to Bethsaida. People brought Him a blind man and begged Him to touch him.
Taking the blind man by the hand, He led him out of the village. He spat into his eyes, laid His hands on him, and asked him, “Do you see anything?”
He looked up and said, “I see people, for I see them like trees, walking.”
Then He laid His hands on his eyes again. The man saw clearly and was restored, and could see everything distinctly.
He sent him home, saying, “Do not even enter the village.”
Jesus and His disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way He questioned His disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?”
They answered Him, saying, “John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But you—who do you say that I am?” Peter answered Him, “Thou art the Christ.”
He strictly warned them to tell no one about Him.
He began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
He spoke this word openly. Peter took Him aside and began rebuking Him.
But He turned, saw His disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying, “Go behind Me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on God’s things, but on human things.”
Calling the crowd to Him with His disciples, He said to them, “If anyone wants to follow behind Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
For what does it benefit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
For what can a person give in exchange for his life?
Whoever is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will certainly not taste death until they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”
After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with Him and brought them up a high mountain privately, alone. He was transfigured before them,
and His clothes became gleaming, exceedingly white, as no cloth bleacher on earth could whiten them.
Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents: one for Thee, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to answer, because they had become terrified.
A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son; listen to Him.”
Suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
As they came down from the mountain, He ordered them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept the word to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
They questioned Him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things. Yet how is it written of the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him.”
When they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes disputing with them.
Immediately the whole crowd saw Him and was greatly astonished. They ran up and greeted Him.
He asked them, “What are you disputing with them?”
One from the crowd answered Him, “Teacher, I brought Thee my son, who has a speechless spirit.
Wherever it seizes him, it dashes him down; he foams, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I told Thy disciples to cast it out, but they did not have the strength.”
He answered them, “O unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to Me.”
They brought him to Him. When the spirit saw Him, it immediately convulsed the boy; falling on the ground, he rolled about, foaming.
He asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood.
Often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if Thou canst do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
Jesus said to him, “‘If Thou canst’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, “I believe; help my unbelief!”
Seeing that a crowd was running together, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Speechless and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him, and enter him no more.”
Crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. The boy became like a dead person, so that most of them said, “He has died.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he stood up.
When He entered a house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?”
He said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer.”
They left there and passed through Galilee, and He did not want anyone to know.
For He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill Him. After He is killed, He will rise after three days.”
But they did not understand the saying, and were afraid to ask Him.
They came to Capernaum. When He was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
They remained silent, for on the way they had discussed with one another who was greatest.
He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.”
He took a child, stood the child among them, and, embracing the child, said to them,
“Whoever receives one such child in My name receives Me; and whoever receives Me does not receive Me but the One who sent Me.”
John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Thy name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”
Jesus said, “Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in My name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of Me.
For whoever is not against us is for us.
Whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in recognition that you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, will certainly not lose his reward.
Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble—it would be better for him if a donkey-driven millstone were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good; but if salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
He rose from there and came into the territory of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Crowds gathered to Him again, and as was His custom, He again taught them.
Pharisees came to Him and asked whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing Him.
He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and dismiss her.”
Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning of creation, ‘He made them male and female.’
‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and cleave to his wife,
and the two shall become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no human separate.”
In the house, the disciples asked Him about this again.
He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
People brought children to Him so that He might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.
When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will certainly not enter it.”
He embraced them and blessed them, laying His hands on them.
As He was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before Him, and asked Him, “Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not bear false witness; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.’”
He said to Him, “Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth.”
Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
But his face fell at the word, and he went away grieved, for he had many possessions.
Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were astounded at His words. But Jesus answered them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
They were exceedingly astonished and said to one another, “Then who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “With humans it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”
Peter began saying to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed Thee.”
Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields for My sake and for the sake of the gospel,
who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, with persecutions—and in the coming age, eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astounded, while those following were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, He began telling them what was going to happen to Him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn Him to death and hand Him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock Him, spit on Him, flog Him, and kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approached Him and said to Him, “Teacher, we want Thee to do for us whatever we ask Thee.”
He said to them, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
They said to Him, “Grant us to sit, one at Thy right and one at Thy left, in Thy glory.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
They said to Him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at My right or at My left is not Mine to give; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
When the ten heard, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to Him and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it is not so among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
They came to Jericho. As He was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a considerable crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
Hearing that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began crying out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out much more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage! Get up; He is calling you.”
He threw off his garment, sprang up, and came to Jesus.
Jesus answered him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” The blind man said to Him, “Rabbouni, that I may see again.”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he saw again and followed Him on the road.
As they drew near Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples
and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. Immediately on entering it, you will find a colt tied, on which no human has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord has need of it, and He will send it back here immediately.’”
They went away and found a colt tied at a door outside on the street, and untied it.
